Standard: The AR system manages loads transmitted to targeted air vehicle. a. Boom Tanker. While coupled to a receiver, the boom system limits axial loads according to ATP-3.3.4.5, Coupled Push Pull Loads paragraph and limits radial loads to less than 750 lbs. b. Drogue Tanker. Hose reel system maintains refueling hose tension such that no excessive slack develops and inadvertent disconnects are avoided. Reception coupling latch forces required to engage the coupling with an MA-2 receiver AR probe nozzle having a 50-lb sleeve force are not greater than 200 lbs with 10 psig static fuel pressure in the coupling. Reception coupling latch forces required to disengage the probe nozzle from the coupling are adjustable between 300 and 550 lbs with 0 psig fuel pressure in the coupling. The force required to separate the nozzle from the coupling, with 50 psig of fuel pressure, with a latch-force setting of 520 ±20 lbs, is not greater than 830 lbs when the disconnect angle of the swivel-ball joint is at the 22.5-degree position. c. Receptacle Receiver. The receptacle system limits the force to disengage the targeted tanker boom nozzle from the receptacle when the receptacle latches fail to actively release from a minimum of 4,800 lbs to a maximum of 9,411 lbs. d. Probe Receiver. The probe system limits the force to depress the nozzle sleeve to the fully open position to less than 45 ±5 lbs and requires 15 lbs or greater force to move the nozzle sleeve to the fully closed position. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Examination of specifications shows boom actuation system is required to manage interface loads. b. Drogue Tanker. Examination of specifications show hose reel and reception coupling are required to manage interface loads. c. Receptacle Receiver. Examination of specifications and receptacle latch design shows expected brute force disconnect loads to be within the required range. d. Probe Receiver. Examination of specifications and nozzle latch design shows latch sleeve operation meets standard. Analysis.
  (1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Analysis and modeling show boom system maintains the required interface loads at all possible boom fuel pressures and extremes of boom envelope. b. Drogue Tanker. Analysis and modeling show hose reel and reception coupling design prevent excess hose slack, minimize negative contacts, and manage interface loads to within the allowable levels. c. Receptacle Receiver. Analysis and modeling show receptacle latch design brute force disconnect loads to be within the required range. d. Probe Receiver. Analysis and modeling show nozzle latch design operates according to the standard. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Laboratory testing of boom system verifies interface loads are within specified values. b. Drogue Tanker. Laboratory testing of hose reel system verifies interface loads are within specified values. Laboratory testing of coupling engagement and disengagement forces verify latch forces are within specified values. c. Receptacle Receiver. Laboratory testing verifies force to disengage with receptacle latches failed closed is within the required range. d. Probe Receiver. Laboratory testing verifies nozzle sleeve operates according to the standard. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight testing with targeted receptacle equipped receivers verifies the boom system allows telescoping in both extension and retraction at rates up to 6.5 ft/s and axial and radial loads are within allowable levels throughout the altitude and air speed AR envelope, boom envelope, and operating fuel pressures. Additional test points include pressure refueling and slipway assisted contacts. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight testing with targeted probe equipped receiver(s) verifies hose tension is maintained, excessive hose slack does not develop, negative contacts are minimized, and inadvertent disconnects due to high hose tension do not occur throughout the altitude and airspeed AR envelope and operating fuel pressures. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight testing with targeted boom equipped tanker verifies controlled tension disconnects with receptacle latches closed result in a tension load between 4,800 lbs and 9,411 lbs. A minimum of 3 tension disconnects should be performed and result in consistent tension load values. If loads are not consistent, additional test points should be accomplished. d. Probe Receiver. Flight testing with targeted drogue equipped tanker verifies engagement, disengagement, and fuel transfer without fuel leakage.
